//: Metadata for the patch-package patches in this directory — one key per patched npm package. Consumed by the orphaned-patch guard (packages/dev-tools/patch-reconcile/check-patches.mjs, run as `npm run lint:patches`) and the renovate-patch-reconcile workflow. Every patches/<pkg>+<version>.patch MUST have an entry here with a matching patchedVersion. When a patch is removed, delete its entry. See patches/README.md.

@zenfs/core.reason: #2146: VCache.ref coalesced DIFFERENT paths onto one vnode when their inodes shared an ino (poisoned indexes carry many ino-0 entries) — the shared inode object cross-stamps size/mode between unrelated files. The patch refuses cross-path coalescing unless the inodes are a genuine hardlink: ino must be nonzero, format bits must match, AND nlink must be > 1 on both sides (#2034). A duplicated real ino with nlink 1 is a poisoned index, not a link — and because every vnode also owns its sparse data cache, two colliding paths open at once returned each other's bytes (8 parallel preview fetches all served the entry file; sequential reads evicted the vnode between calls and were correct). (The patch also used to carry an Index._alloc() hunk for zen-fs/core#312 — the Math.max spread of 2x entryCount arguments that threw RangeError('Maximum call stack size exceeded') on every createFile/mkdir once the OPFS index grew large. That fix shipped upstream in 2.6.5, which now reduces instead of spreading and memoizes the last id, so the hunk is gone; tests/fs/zenfs-alloc-overflow-upstream.test.ts pins the upstream behavior.)
@zenfs/core.removeWhen: Remove once zen-fs/core#314 ships — @zenfs/core must refuse to share a vnode across paths for non-hardlink inodes. (The patch also used to rewrite `globalThis.__zenfs__` into an own-property copy so a probe could enumerate it; upstream declined that in https://github.com/zen-fs/core/issues/310 — the global is deliberately minimal — so that hunk is gone and consumers must probe by existence plus the `_version` export instead.)
@zenfs/core.verify: npm run test -w @slicc/webapp -- zenfs-ino-collision-patch virtual-fs-concurrent-read zenfs-alloc-overflow-upstream

@zenfs/dom.reason: #2146: WebAccessFS minted ino:0 inodes in stat's ENOENT recovery and _loadMetadata's reality branch; thousands of ino-0 index entries collapse onto one VFS vnode-cache slot, stamping one file's size/mode onto another path on sync (phantom directories, sibling-size truncation). The patch allocates unique ino/data pairs at both sites. Those allocations must set nlink: 1 — ZenFS's Inode constructor warns on every ino!=0/nlink==0 inode and kerium retains every log entry, so leaving nlink unset flooded the in-memory log on every inode materialization until its backing Set hit V8's 2^24 cap and every FS op threw 'Set maximum size exceeded' (2026-08-18 VFS-offline incident). ALSO (#2157): a 0-byte file never reached OPFS at all — the VFS vnode only calls the backend's `write` for dirty BYTE ranges and an empty file has none, so `IndexFS.createFile` put an inode in the index and no FileSystemFileHandle was ever created. `stat`/`exists` then answered from the index while `unlink` raised ENOENT from `removeEntry`, and ZenFS clears the vnode cache only AFTER a successful unlink, so the entry reverted to existing: `rm` could not delete a 0-byte file at all, and `rm -f` / `rm -rf` reported success while deleting nothing. The patch materializes the handle in `createFile` (every indexed file then exists on disk, and the first write skips the failing lookup it used to pay for) and makes `remove` tolerate an already-absent OPFS entry — IndexFS has already validated existence against the authoritative index, so an entry it knows but OPFS does not was otherwise undeletable forever: the phantom-deletion class. The `createFile` insert is rolled back when OPFS refuses the create (quota, permission): `super.createFile` has already added the inode, so leaving it on the error path would recreate the same divergence from the other side — `stat` reporting a file that was never created, the next create hitting EEXIST, and a flush able to persist the phantom into the sidecar. (The patch also used to carry a `keepExistingData: !fullWrite` hunk in `write`: WebAccessFS copied the whole existing file into the swap file on every write and nothing ever truncated the handle, so a shrink left its tail in OPFS quota forever. That fix shipped upstream in 1.2.11 (zen-fs/dom#42) — `WebAccessFS.touch` now truncates the handle, and because Vnode.sync pre-truncates before flushing dirty ranges, an O_TRUNC rewrite reaches `write` with a 0-byte file on disk and the copy is free. The hunk is gone; tests/fs/zenfs-dom-truncate-upstream.test.ts pins the upstream behavior.)
@zenfs/dom.removeWhen: Split by hunk. The ino-allocation hunks track zen-fs/dom#43, filed with a failing test against zen-fs/dom's own ponyfill suite; remove them once WebAccess allocates real ino/data pairs at both minting sites. The zero-byte createFile/remove hunks are still unfiled — reproduced on 1.2.11: writeFile of an empty buffer never creates the OPFS handle, so unlink then throws ENOENT for a file stat says exists.

kerium.reason: kerium's log() retains EVERY entry in a module-global List (a plain Set underneath) with no cap or rotation — even entries below the output threshold that are never printed (default minLevel is ALERT). A long-lived kernel worker under log pressure (e.g. ZenFS's per-inode nlink warning) eventually hits V8's 2^24-element Set cap, after which entries.add throws RangeError('Set maximum size exceeded') into every logging caller — every ZenFS op failed and the VFS went offline (2026-08-18 incident). The patch evicts the oldest entry beyond a 10,000-entry ring so the backlog stays bounded.
kerium.removeWhen: Remove once kerium bounds its log backlog upstream (ring buffer or opt-in retention).

isomorphic-git.reason: #2710/#2735: share in-flight pack SHA-1 verification across concurrent readers and use each call's external-delta reader so a persistent pack cache neither re-hashes a pack nor retains a stale command-scoped filesystem closure.
isomorphic-git.removeWhen: Remove once isomorphic-git memoizes in-flight pack verification and GitPackIndex.read uses the current call's external-delta reader.

just-bash.reason: curl formats the response for stdout (`N(...)` → latin1 decode of the WHOLE body via `Buffer.from(body).toString('binary')`) BEFORE checking `-o`/`-O`, then discards the string. In the browser the `buffer` polyfill's latin1Slice builds that string one `+=` per byte, so every downloaded byte costs a ~32-byte V8 cons-string node: a 250 MB `curl -o` needed ~8 GB of V8 heap and crashed the leader tab (renderer OOM → Inspector.targetCrashed). The patch skips the stdout formatting when the body is going to a file (unless `-v`, which still prints it), so `curl -o` costs the body bytes, not a string copy of them.
just-bash.removeWhen: Remove once just-bash's curl only formats the body for stdout when it will be printed (or streams `-o` output to the fs).
